area: mac-verify.sh — the cli-anything-browser posture row, on a Mac where the harness has never been installed
finding: The browser-harness security check ran unconditionally, because its precondition was the wrong one. The old guard was `if [ -x "$CAH_POSTURE" ]` — posture.sh is checked into this repo, so that test is true on every machine that has the repo at all, including one where nothing has ever been installed. On such a Mac the check printed `FAIL cli-anything-browser posture — posture.sh check failed — run it directly to see which control is off`. No control was off. Nothing was there. This is the first FAIL Steven would meet on a first run, it names a security control, and it is wrong for exactly the reason it gives — the class of row that teaches a person to skip the verifier, and then the verifier is not read on the day a control really is off.
evidence: Run against a simulated HOME with nothing installed (Linux, 2026-09-23): the row fired as a FAIL alongside the eight `cli-anything-* not installed` FAILs that already said the harness was absent, taking the FAIL count to 16. Running posture.sh check by hand in the same conditions shows why: its first line is `FAIL F-P1-05 not checked: no interpreter at <venv>/bin/python`, i.e. it reports a missing interpreter through the same non-zero exit it uses for a disabled control, and mac-verify.sh could not tell the two apart.
fix: APPLIED. The check is gated on `[ -x "$CAH_VENV/bin/python" ]`; with no harness the row is `info … harness venv not built yet — nothing to prove`. Proved in both directions on Linux: after a real install of all eight harnesses into a simulated HOME the row is `ok … all in force`, and moving the pinned DOMShell node_modules aside puts it back to FAIL. So the FAIL is still reachable and now only means what it says. Never run on macOS.

area: MAC-SETUP.sh and mac-verify.sh — F-P6-03 follow-through, the skill loops
finding: VERIFIED CORRECT, both scripts, including the empty-directory guard. The hard-coded nine is gone; both enumerate `$REPO_DIR/.claude/skills/*/`. The guard that matters is the one against the enumeration's own failure mode: a glob that matches nothing leaves the pattern literal, `[ -d ]` skips it, the loop body never runs, and a naive 'no missing skills' test would then report a green light for nothing at all. Both scripts count first and judge second — MAC-SETUP.sh on `skill_n`, mac-verify.sh on `skill_seen` — and both call zero a failure.
evidence: Executed on Linux 2026-09-23 in four conditions, using copies of both scripts beside a `.claude/skills` that was (a) the real 22 and (b) empty, and (c,d) absent entirely. Real repo: MAC-SETUP.sh reports 'all 22 vendored skills present', mac-verify.sh prints 22 `ok skill <name>` rows. Empty AND absent, both scripts: MAC-SETUP.sh `FAILED no skills found … (empty or missing — pull the repo again)` and exit 1; mac-verify.sh `FAIL skills — an empty directory is not a pass`. No condition produced a false pass.
fix: None needed. Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it. One stale consequence was found and fixed elsewhere: MAC-INSTALL-tooling.md's order-of-operations still told Steven nine vendored skills load with the repo.

area: MAC-SETUP.sh — three steps reporting something they had not checked
finding: Three `installed` messages asserted more than the run had established. (a) The whatsapp-cli step reported '+ symlink in ~/.local/bin' whether or not `ln` succeeded — this is the line carrying the pre-existing SC2015 note. (b) The cli-anything step reported 'cli-anything-hub (cli-hub) 0.4.1 verified' without checking that anything landed or what version it was; 0.4.1 was verified in a cloud sandbox on 2026-09-22, not by this run, and the word 'verified' in an installer's own output reads as this run's finding. (c) The cli-anything-harnesses step reported 'eight harnesses … + symlinks' on the strength of one `uv pip install` exit status, with the eight symlinks made by `ln -sf … || true`.
evidence: Read from source. On (a), the SC2015 judgement: `A && B || C` is NOT a real bug at that line, because C is `true` and the `||` exists only to keep `set -e` from killing the run — the case shellcheck warns about (C running when A succeeded) is a no-op here. The line was wrong for a different reason the warning does not name, which is why it is fixed rather than suppressed. shellcheck now reports zero findings on MAC-SETUP.sh at default, where it previously reported this one.
fix: APPLIED. (a) Split into two independent best-effort commands; the message says which of the two landed. (b) Presence checked with `uv_tool_present cli-hub` the way codeburn/omniroute/headroom already do, and the version read from the installed tool — captured with `|| true` inside the substitution, because a bare assignment takes the substitution's status and a missing cli-hub would otherwise abort the script under `set -e`. (c) Console scripts and symlinks counted separately: 8/8 built or it is a failure, symlinks reported as a count. Proved by a real install of all eight into a simulated HOME on Linux: 8/8 and 8/8, second run 'already present', rebuilds nothing. Never run on macOS.

area: MAC-SETUP.sh — `--only=` and `--skip=` with nothing after the equals sign
finding: `./MAC-SETUP.sh --only=` appended a bare space to ONLY. A space is non-empty, so the `[ -n "$ONLY" ]` filter engaged, but it matched no step name, so every step was filtered out; and the validation loop `for n in $ONLY $SKIP` iterates zero times over whitespace, so no 'unknown step' error fired either. The run printed a full, clean summary reading 'WOULD INSTALL: none / FAILED: none' and exited 0. A typo that produces a successful-looking run which installed nothing is the quietest kind of false reassurance: the exit code, the summary and the absence of errors all agree, and all three are wrong.
evidence: Executed on Linux 2026-09-23: `--only=` exit 0, zero step headers. Contrast `--only` with no value at all, which correctly dies on `${1:?}` with exit 1, and an unknown step name, which correctly exits 2.
fix: APPLIED. Both `--only=` and `--skip=` with an empty value now print the reason and exit 2, matching the unknown-step path. Re-tested: exit 2 for both; `--only=codeburn` still runs exactly one step.

area: The Phase A hand-run sequence in the personal-involvement runbook — `./MAC-SETUP.sh --skip omniroute`
finding: Phase A reads as five quick flag exercises. Its fourth line is not one. `./MAC-SETUP.sh --skip omniroute` has no `--dry-run`, so it is a full real install of the other 24 steps: two git clones, four venvs, a global npm install, a playwright chromium download, a `claude plugin install` into the live Claude Code user scope (F-R3-10), and `npm ci` for the pinned DOMShell copy. Two further consequences will read as breakage when they are not. The omniroute step is the only step that writes `~/.config/claude-runner/role`, installs `claude-auto` and installs `probe.sh` — so skipping it means Phase A's fifth line, `./mac-verify.sh`, reports `FAIL omniroute`, `FAIL claude-auto`, `FAIL probe.sh` and `NEED claude-runner role`, and exits 1. That exit 1 is the correct consequence of line four, not a fault. Separately, line three, `./MAC-SETUP.sh --only codeburn`, presupposes node/npm: on a Mac where Homebrew has not been installed yet it exits 1 with `FAILED npm missing` before any prerequisite step has been allowed to run.
evidence: Executed on Linux 2026-09-23. `--skip omniroute --dry-run` prints 24 step headers, no omniroute header, no claude-runner/role line, no claude-auto line, and 40 would-run commands including both clones, the chromium download and the plugin install. mac-verify.sh against a simulated HOME with exactly the omniroute artefacts removed produces the four rows above and exit 1. `--only codeburn` with npm off PATH: `FAILED npm missing`, exit 1.
fix: NOT A CODE CHANGE — every one of these behaviours is correct; the runbook's framing is what needs the words. Handed to the runbook owner: say that line four is the real install and how long it takes; say that lines four and five together are expected to end in exit 1 with those four specific rows, and that this proves --skip worked rather than that something broke; put `--only codeburn` after a prerequisite run, or say it needs node. A safer Phase A that demonstrates the same three flags without installing anything: `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--dry-run --only codeburn`, `--dry-run --skip omniroute`, then `./mac-verify.sh` as the before picture.

area: Both scripts — what remains unverifiable without a real Mac, claim by claim
finding: Everything in this audit was executed on Linux. The scripts have still never run on macOS, and the gap is not uniform — some claims are platform-independent and are now genuinely proved, others cannot be touched from here at all. Proved and platform-independent: argument parsing, step selection, the REFUSED and DECLINED guards, both skill loops and their empty-directory guards, idempotence of the dry-run and of the real file-writing path, file modes, the absence of any written secret value, the eight-harness install and its PEP 420 namespace, the posture check in both directions, and every cron and UTC derivation. Depends on macOS and is NOT proved: `brew install` of uv/pipx/node; `stat -f '%OLp'` (the BSD branch of filemode() — only the GNU branch ran here); every launchctl and `com.stevenshearrill` agent row; every runnerctl row; Full Disk Access and Accessibility, and therefore whatsapp-cli's send path; the WhatsApp desktop-app URL scheme; `~/Library/Logs/vanessa-setup` (the log directory was created under a simulated HOME on Linux, which proves the code path, not the location); and macOS /bin/bash 3.2 itself — the scripts are written for it and avoid its known gaps, but every execution here was bash 5.2, so a 3.2-only incompatibility would not have been caught.
evidence: Every command in this engagement ran on Linux 6.18 with bash 5.2.21, shellcheck 0.9.0, against simulated HOME directories. The non-Darwin guard had to be overridden with VANESSA_SETUP_ALLOW_NON_DARWIN=1 for every real-path test, which is the script correctly saying so.
fix: None. Recorded per claim rather than as a blanket disclaimer, so the first real run on the Mac can be read as the test it is. The single highest-value thing that first run proves is bash 3.2 compatibility, because it is the one class of failure nothing here could have caught.
